synopsis: PR/FAQ presents a proposed finished product through a press release and accompanying questions-and-answers; working backwards means writing these before building, to clarify who benefits and what must be true [f16455, f16456, f16457]. Chapter 12 places it among practitioner communication formats, including the Pyramid Principle, BLUF, six-page narratives, the Five Case Model and Decision Quality, but no controlled evidence was found that these presentation formats improve technical-program approval or success [f9851, f9853, f16467]. The six-page narrative is recommended as a suitable template for the heavy off-road collision mitigation validation plan, with a documented six-page limit and silent reading at the start of meetings rather than slides [f9980, f9989, f16458]. Planning guidance also recommends a 1–2-page executive decision brief and a fifteen-section plan with appendices; alternative overall lengths—12–15 main-body pages or a two-page brief plus roughly 25–35 core pages—are explicitly opinion rather than demonstrated optima [f10152, f16465, f16466]. The claimed practical value is answering reviewers' actual questions, especially what would show the authors are wrong; assertion-evidence slides have limited evidence for improved comprehension, which is distinct from evidence of improved approval or programme success [f16468, f9859, f16464, f16467].
